chapters.text: I took the coin out and paid. The story has just begun. I stayed on the road and said the next words out loud.
Then another voice paid a dollar and spoke. The road kept going. The story went on, just a bit more.
Footsteps echoed softly where the shadows thinned.

The thinning showed a lantern nobody was holding, set on a stone where the trees had stopped arguing. I stood still and listened. The footsteps did not come closer. They circled, soft, as if whoever made them already knew the road and was only checking that I had stayed. The lantern flame leaned toward me, then away, and in that lean I saw the last porch light far behind, no bigger than a pin. Ahead, the dark had a seam in it. I put one hand out. The seam was warm.
